Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee: Terri Koch (E009), requests admin access to Payroll.

Notes from team memory:
- Note 1 (HR?): role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment: full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll. Admin only if role owns system; Engineer doesn't own Payroll, so max is write. Recommend write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment: Security DB authoritative, contractor with basic training. Contractors limited to read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Recommend read.

Conflicting information between HR and Security. The Security note says Security DB is authoritative for employment type. So employee is a contractor with basic security training.

For contractors: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. So maximum is read (since basic training).

Requested level: admin. Above maximum. Grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Employee is a contractor with basic security training (per Security DB, authoritative), so maximum access is read. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so grant read.
